title: Reversible rule 37R does not obey the Second Law

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Reversible rule 37R does not obey the Second Law

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The reversible cellular automaton rule 37R, even as a closed system, shows neither a systematic trend toward increasing randomness nor simple predictable behavior, but fluctuates indefinitely between more and less ordered states, so it does not obey the Second Law for practical purposes.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: There is, I believe, no choice but to conclude that for practical purposes rule 37R simply does not obey the Second Law.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 9, “Fundamental Physics”; section “Irreversibility and the Second Law of Thermodynamics” (from p. 441), p. 453. Scope: the second-order reversible elementary cellular automaton rule 37R in finite closed regions

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch09-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.80

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The rule is explicit and inexpensive to simulate, so substantial evidence is available immediately. The indefinite statement and the phrase 'for practical purposes' prevent finite computation from fully resolving it.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Simulate rule 37R over many finite sizes, initial conditions, and long durations, measuring entropy, compressibility, and recurrence. A robust monotone rise to equilibrium would refute the claim, while persistent bidirectional fluctuations would support it over the sampled regimes.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Finite simulations cannot establish indefinite behavior.

Randomness and order admit several inequivalent measures.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The rule, the closed finite setting, and the alternatives (monotonic randomization, or simple repetition as in rules 0R and 90R) are fully specified, and Wolfram already records a concrete period for one run. Re-simulation with a fixed disorder statistic can confirm or refute the non-monotonic, non-ergodic behavior at practical sizes. The thermodynamic-limit reading of the Second Law is the main residual interpretation, not a missing dataset.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Simulate second-order rule 37R on finite rings from many initial conditions and track a disorder measure, the recurrence time, and the fraction of the state space visited. The claim is confirmed if disorder fluctuates without a systematic rise and orbits stay non-ergodic and non-trivially long; it is refuted if disorder rises monotonically to equilibrium or the evolution is the short-period repetitive type.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A cellular-automaton disorder measure is only a proxy for thermodynamic entropy.

Any finite reversible system eventually recurs, so 'indefinitely' has to be read relative to the recurrence time.
